edges.rationale: SMTP can only be understood as the transfer protocol connecting the mail servers defined in the architecture; the client/server roles and direct delivery between servers presuppose the user agent/mail server model and message queues.

edges.dependent: Mail Access Protocols: POP3, IMAP, and HTTP
edges.rationale: Access protocols are defined by their role in the architecture: retrieving mail from the recipient's mail server. Without the mail-server/mailbox model, POP3 and IMAP have no context.

The message-format discussion (7-bit ASCII restrictions of SMTP motivating MIME) builds directly on SMTP's command dialogue and its content restrictions; MIME is introduced as a response to SMTP's limitations.
Header lines such as Received: only make sense in light of the message's journey through mail servers described in the architecture.
